name: Name
title: Kubernetes
intro: Let your chats and agents read a Kubernetes cluster and, with your confirmation, change it. Each connection is one context of one cluster.
limits: A chat can do what the credential of the connection may do, inside the policy an administrator sets below. Use a service account with only the RBAC rights the task needs. In the mode "Runs at once" no one confirms a change before it is made.

method.label: Credential
method.hint: The credential is kept sealed and never shown again.

kubeconfigHelp: Paste a kubeconfig with embedded data. Credential plugins (exec, auth-provider), file paths, proxies, user names and passwords are not supported.
tooLargeHint: This is too large. Keep only one context with kubectl config view --minify --flatten --context={{context}}, or use a service account token.

problem.tooLarge: The kubeconfig is larger than 16384 bytes.
problem.plugin: This kubeconfig uses a credential plugin (exec or auth-provider). The add-on runs no program: use a token or a client certificate.
problem.fileRef: This kubeconfig names a file (certificate-authority, client-certificate, client-key or tokenFile). Embed the data instead: kubectl config view --flatten.
problem.insecure: This kubeconfig turns off the check of the server certificate (insecure-skip-tls-verify). The add-on always checks it.
problem.proxy: This kubeconfig uses a proxy (proxy-url). The add-on connects directly.
problem.basicAuth: This kubeconfig logs in with a user name and a password. Use a token or a client certificate.

contextHelp: The context of the kubeconfig that this connection uses. The others are ignored.
serverHelp: The https URL of the API server, with no path: https://cluster.example:6443.
serverShape: Write an https URL with no path.
caHelp: The certificate of the cluster's CA. Leave it empty if the server certificate is signed by a public CA.
tokenHelp: A bearer token, for example of a service account: kubectl create token <name>.
keyLong: The server and the context are too long together, or the context has a space.
checkSeveral: The check runs when you have one Kubernetes connection, because a check from this page cannot tell which one you mean. In a chat, enable the connections in the Tools menu.
noCluster: No cluster: this connection reaches nothing.

confirmDelete.title: Delete {{name}}?
confirmDelete.message: Your chats can no longer reach this cluster, and the kubeconfig saved with it is deleted. To set it up again you must paste it again.

check.title: Check of {{name}}
check.cut: The cluster sent more rules than the check shows.
check.incomplete: The cluster could not list every rule: the credential may do more than this.
check.none: No rules: the credential may do nothing in this namespace.
check.unauthorized: The cluster refused the credential. Paste a new kubeconfig or token.
check.forbidden: The credential may not run the check. An administrator of the cluster can grant it.
check.unsafe: The add-on cannot use this kubeconfig. Edit the connection and paste one with embedded data and no plugin.
check.mismatch: The kubeconfig has no context of this connection, or it points at another server.
check.unreachable: The cluster could not be reached, or its certificate is not trusted. Check the server and the CA.
check.nocred: This connection has no kubeconfig. Edit it and paste one.
check.failed: The check did not finish. Try again in a moment.

setup.title: How to set it up
setup.step1: Make a service account for LocalAI, with a Role or ClusterRole that grants only what the task needs.
setup.step2: Make a kubeconfig with one context: kubectl config view --minify --flatten --context=<name>. Or make a token: kubectl create token <name>.
setup.step3: Paste it here and press Save. The check shows the version of the cluster and the RBAC rules of the credential.
setup.step4: Leave the mode on Asks you first until you have read the limits on this page.

writeMode.label: What the agent may change in this cluster
writeMode.hint: Reading is always allowed. A change needs a mode other than Off, and the policy of the cluster must allow the tool.

line.propose: Each change waits for your OK.

note.off: Changes are off: this connection only reads.
note.propose: Each change waits in your approvals with the object and the diff until you confirm it, unless you chose Always runs for that tool below.
note.auto: Changes run at once with no confirmation. Choose this only for a cluster where a wrong change does no harm.

tool.exec: Run a command in a container

policy.title: What chats may do in each cluster
policy.intro: An administrator sets the policy of each cluster. The add-on enforces it on every call, whether a person confirmed the call or not.
policy.loadFailed: The policy could not be loaded.
policy.saveFailed: The policy could not be saved.
policy.readOnly: Only an administrator can change the policy.
policy.broken: The saved policy could not be read. Until an administrator saves again, every cluster gets no namespace, no write and hidden Secret values. When you save, the damaged file is kept aside and a new file starts with that policy as the default: enter the policy of every other cluster again.
policy.invalid: These saved entries do not name a server the add-on accepts, so they never apply: {{list}}. The next save removes them.
policy.saved: Saved. The next call uses the new policy.
policy.clusterHint: Each cluster is named by its server URL, with the contexts of the connections that use it. The default policy applies to every cluster with no policy of its own.
policy.noClusters: No cluster yet. Save a connection first.
policy.ownPolicy: This cluster has its own policy.
policy.defaultPolicy: This cluster has no policy of its own and uses the default policy.
policy.defaultTarget: Default for clusters with no policy
policy.notConfigured: Not configured: writes are off. This cluster uses the default policy, which allows no write, until an administrator saves a policy for it.
policy.noNamespace: No namespace: reads and writes are off. This cluster gets a policy that allows no namespace, until an administrator saves a policy for it.
policy.defaultSet: An administrator set this default. It applies to every cluster with no policy of its own.
policy.defaultBuiltin: The built-in default: reads in every namespace, Secret values included, and no write. It applies to every cluster with no policy of its own.
policy.legacy: These saved policies use the old key per context and disagree for one server, so they no longer apply: {{list}}. Save a policy for that server.
policy.namespacesHint: The namespaces the tools may read and change. * allows every namespace. Objects outside any namespace (nodes) need *.
policy.nsEmpty: Name at least one namespace, or *.
policy.nsShape: "{{entry}}" is not a namespace name: lower case letters, digits and -, at most 63.
policy.toolsHint: A tool that is off is refused, whatever the write mode and the approvals are.
policy.powerful: Powerful: runs any command in a container, and its output is not filtered.
policy.secretsHint: On by default: the model sees Secret values unless an administrator turns this off. When off, the read tools and the diffs of writes show the keys of a Secret and hide its values, a json patch may not copy, move or test a value, and apply may not set a hidden value again. This does not cover what workloads show: a pod that a chat creates to mount or print a Secret, exec, and logs can still show values, and a patch preview can confirm a guessed value. Turn off apply, patch and exec to close those paths.
policy.secretsWarn: A chat that reads a Secret value sends it to the model and keeps it in the chat history.

approval.title: Ask before changing
approval.intro: By default every change waits for your confirmation. For each tool you can choose not to be asked. The choice is yours alone, it applies to all your Kubernetes connections, and only this page can change it.

line.ask: A card waits for your OK.

approval.warn: With Always runs, a chat makes the change at once, with no card to confirm.
approval.warnExec: With Always runs, a chat can run any command in a container at once.
approval.who: Always runs holds for your own chats and for messaging senders you paired with the bot. Everyone else is still asked.
approval.needsWrite: A connection set to Read only changes nothing, whatever you choose here. The policy of the cluster still decides which tools work.
approval.loadFailed: Your choice could not be read. Reload the page to try again.
approval.saveFailed: Your choice could not be saved. The earlier choice is still in force.
approval.saved: Saved. The next call follows it.

card.title: {{tool}}: {{target}}
card.physical: This changes a real cluster as soon as you confirm.
card.noDiff: The dry run shows no change.
card.diffCut: Diff cut: the change is larger than shown.
card.commandNote: The command runs as these {{count}} separate arguments, with no shell unless the first one is a shell.
